verdict.rationale: FFmpeg has no GUI. Its primary interface is the ffmpeg CLI, which sits on documented libraries (libavfilter, libavformat, libavdevice) with nightly Doxygen docs and code examples, so programmatic access to the same pipeline exists. Features like IAMF appear in both the library and the CLI. However, no source states full parity, there is no OpenAPI or HTTP API, and a user reports that libav API docs and examples are sparse compared to the CLI. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that the library API covers everything the CLI does, clear up-to-date API tutorials, and independent confirmation of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: libavfilter provides means to alter decoded audio and video through a directed graph of connected filters.
libavformat implements streaming protocols, container formats and basic I/O access.
The libavformat library can now read and write IAMF (Immersive Audio) files. The ffmpeg CLI tool can configure IAMF structure with the new -stream_group option.
